title: PanopticonVerdictBundle
description: One verify-cell reply: every verdict the advisor was handed, plus the cell-identity stamp. The advisor verdict is INLINED rather than referenced -- a host CLI given this as a constrained-output schema resolves no external reference -- and tests/test_verify_schema_fields.py pins the inlined copy to skill/reference/advisor-verdict-schema.json.

run_id.description: Optional (#1054): the tool-advisor path echoes no run_id (the driver writes no verify-queue.json for it and match_verdict binds on finding_id alone), and the advisor prompt example omits it. Allowed if a host stamps it, never required.

schema_version.description: Format/schema version of the advisor verdict.

evidence_scope.description: Backup round only (#1638 P16): the bounded evidence closure this advisor was granted -- the claim files, the producers their evidence named, and their one-hop in-repo imports -- copied verbatim from the prompt's "Evidence granted for this check (bounded closure)" section. It records what the advisor could actually read, so a thin verdict can be told from a thin grant. `cap`/`truncated` bound ONE claim's closure; `entry_cap`/`entry_truncated` bound the closure EXTRAS across every claim in this check. `floor_count` is how many of the granted files are claim files, which no cap bounds -- so a grant larger than `entry_cap` with `entry_truncated: false` is a large floor, not an inconsistency. Optional: the primary and tool rounds are granted no closure and record none.

missing_evidence.description: Files this advisor needed and was NOT granted (#1638 P16). Meaningful only on a NEEDS_MORE_INFO verdict, where it marks an evidence-SCOPE failure: the finding keeps evidence.status `backup_scope_limited`, the primary CONFIRMED stands, and the report names what the backup could not see. A NEEDS_MORE_INFO without it is a substantive one and keeps its existing meaning.

_panopticon.description: Cell-identity block: the run_id/group/domain/stage of the entry that asked for this bundle. REQUIRED -- persist refuses a bundle whose stamp contradicts the entry -- and filled in by the driver for a return-persist reply that omits it (`stamped_by: "controller"`); a self-written bundle must carry it. Only run_id is required: the driver stamps the identity keys it declared on the entry, and `role` -- the agent's own name for what it was -- is not one of them.

stamped_by.description: Present when the DRIVER filled a missing key of this stamp (D10 ruling 4); never written by the agent.

schema_version.description: Format/schema version of the verdict bundle.
